Japanese_movement.refuel: Protected Guimaras top-off closes during the morning; no rush that leaves the main carrier groups underfueled.
Japanese_movement.sortie: Main carrier/surface echelons depart Guimaras/central-Philippines system during the morning-to-midday window and move east through the Visayan/San Bernardino route in staggered battle groups.
Japanese_movement.formation_policy: The force does not move as one dense column. Carrier groups, heavy reserve and oilers use staggered sectors/intervals to reduce submarine and single-contact risk.
Japanese_movement.oilers: Oilers remain outside the carrier tactical formation and proceed toward protected rendezvous/standby areas with dedicated escorts.

Shiratsuyu_accident_gate.historical_event: Historical 14 Jun false-torpedo-warning collision with Seiyo Maru sank Shiratsuyu.
Shiratsuyu_accident_gate.branch_result: NO EVENT / SHIRATSUYU SURVIVES 14 JUN centerline.
Shiratsuyu_accident_gate.reason: The exact oiler escort timing, route and formation are changed by the branch's earlier concentration and staggered logistics posture. Improved contact classification reduces false-alarm maneuver risk but is not treated as accident immunity.

US_submarine_contact.result: Late 14 Jun a US submarine obtains a credible major-fleet contact on an eastbound Japanese echelon near the Philippine exit approaches. Composition is incomplete: carriers are probable/strongly suspected, but eleven-deck total and exact battle-group split are not yet resolved.
US_submarine_contact.quality: MAJOR-FLEET-SORTIE QUALITY, not full OOB/weapon-quality track.
US_submarine_contact.attack: No successful torpedo attack on the main body on 14 Jun; Japanese ASW screen and geometry force the contact submarine to prioritize reporting/recontact.
US_submarine_contact.effect: Spruance/Mitscher receive warning that a major Japanese fleet is moving east, broadly preserving the historical strategic warning function even though the branch's departure and contact clock differ.
